question: What Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State Governor has the authority to reserve a bill for the consideration of the President?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 200.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 200, provides the Governor of a state has the **authority to reserve certain bills** passed by the state legislature for consideration of the President of India.
 
• The Governor **can reserve** bill if:
 
 
• The bill may conflict with central laws.
 
• The bill concerns an issue of national importance.
 
• The bill might endanger the position of the High Court.
 
 
 
• The bill can also send for reconsideration
 
• The **Money bill** cannot be reserved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 201 **involves the** process to be followed **if the bill is reserved for consideration of President of India.
 
• **Article 267 **provides for the **creation of Contingency Funds**, both at the Union and at the State level.
 
• **Article 181** covers the procedure for **removal of Speaker or Deputy Speaker of Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Article 190** provides conditions for disqualification/vacation of members from Legislative Assembly. The conditions are:
 
 
• if a person is chosen a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State or the Legislature of two or more States, he/she has to vacate one seat.
 
• a member is absent for more than 60 days without permission of speaker of the house.
